R1 (K4218; member-roster R76, R29): a claimed founder is an active member and still takes no routed task; the task goes to the first administrator after her, and with none it is unassigned (control: unclaimed)
R1 (N322): an exhausted task id space keeps the event, its waiting entry carrying record-core R62's code, check and detail
R1, R3: an act given no instant stamps the instance's clock, not the wall's
R1: the task-drain consumer is due every firing, wakes at the delay while events wait (backstop after an idle tick), and drains
R18 (K2038): after a tick that drains nothing the wake backs off by each event's own attempts, and past the retry limit an unfiled capture is retried hourly, never dropped
R1 (T36): the drain reads capture's queue in pages past each page's last cursor; a waiting event does not use up limit, so limit waiting events at the head never hide a filed one behind them
R18 (T36): the wake's reading of the waiting events pages with after as R1 does, so the earliest due instant is taken over every waiting event, not the first page alone
R2: taskList lists visible tasks newest first, filtered, bounded with truncated, and counts over the visible set
R3: taskForward's refusals in order, then forwarded with its history; taskResolve's, then resolved; both per item as a set

R3 (T38, N793; K231): taskForward to no active member answers NO_SUCH_MEMBER through membership's noSuchMember (its R121, C-96.47), member the to asked, its row and sentence membership's; nothing is written
R3: an administrator resolves another member's task; the founder's session is one
R3, R7 (N382): the task-actor fence answers its own code, TASK_NOT_YOURS, never intent's NOT_YOURS, and each refusal's code keys its own row
R8, R17: tasks and the check tables are declared to the whole-store purge only: a bundle's purge leaves them, the whole-store purge clears them
R9: no answer names a bundle the viewer may not see, and no count reveals one
R9 (D54; K2408, K2442): an administrator neither invited nor joined to a hidden project is answered as any outsider; a discoverable project, or an invited administrator, sees its tasks whole
R1 (K2575, D54): the administrator fallback picks the earliest active administrator membership R80 admits to the subject; with none, unassigned
R3 (K2575, D54; membership R60, R80): an administrator's override holds only where the actor sees the subject; else NO_SUCH_TASK, never TASK_NOT_YOURS naming the assignee
